question: Is any repair shop an outlier on cost?

input.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments WHERE load_batch LIKE 'nightly-%' GROUP BY 1), c AS (SELECT c.repair_shop_id, c.cause, coalesce(p.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount inc FROM claims c LEFT JOIN p USING(claim_id) WHERE c.repair_shop_id IS NOT NULL), s AS (SELECT repair_shop_id, count(*) n, avg(inc) avg_cost FROM c GROUP BY 1) SELECT s.repair_shop_id, r.name, r.state, r.metro, r.network_status, n, round(avg_cost,0) avg_cost, round((avg_cost-avg(avg_cost) OVER())/stddev(avg_cost) OVER(),2) z FROM s JOIN repair_shops r USING(repair_shop_id) ORDER BY avg_cost DESC LIMIT 8

report.interpretation: I read 'outlier on cost' as average incurred cost per claim (paid plus open reserve) for auto claims handled by each repair shop. Only collision, glass and hail claims have a shop. All loss dates are included. I compared each shop with the others and also adjusted for its mix of causes, because glass claims are cheap. I excluded the 159 duplicate payment rows from the March 2026 reload batch.
report.answer: Yes, one shop stands out: Campbell Body Works (RS-041, Chicago, non-preferred). Across 79 claims it averages $5,774 per claim. That is 2.7 standard deviations above the average shop, and the highest of all 48 shops. After adjusting for its mix of causes, it is about 28% above expected ($4,506). The next highest shops are Ray Body Works (RS-048, $5,187), Hughes Auto Repair (RS-014, $5,120) and Fletcher Collision Center (RS-004, $5,092). These are only 1.5 to 1.7 standard deviations out, so I don't treat them as clear outliers. Non-preferred shops overall are not more expensive than preferred shops. For collision, non-preferred averages $5,401 and preferred $5,331. So Campbell's cost looks like a shop-specific issue and not a network effect. Campbell has only 79 claims, so it is worth a review but not proof of a problem.

findings.claim: Non-preferred shops are not more expensive than preferred shops for the same cause, so network status doesn't explain the outlier.

data_quality_issues.issue: 159 duplicate payment rows from the reload-2026-03-14 batch, loaded outside the nightly batches.
data_quality_issues.impact: They would overstate paid amounts for the affected claims. I excluded that batch, assuming it only duplicates earlier payments.

data_quality_issues.issue: Some payment amounts are very large (322 above about $25k, the largest $237k).
data_quality_issues.impact: A few large payments can move a small shop's average. I did not remove them.

proposed_actions.title: Review Campbell Body Works (RS-041) estimates and invoices
proposed_actions.reason: Its claim costs are about 28% above expected for its mix of causes, and it is a non-preferred shop in Chicago. A review of its invoices or a network invitation could be considered.

open_questions: Should I look at cost by cause (for example collision only) or by region or metro for Campbell and the other top shops?
